oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer assertions and access tokens are not documented as one-time-use by default; replay prevention depends on specific grant context or additional policy, not generic JWT state tracking.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC token endpoint and general JWT/OAuth behavior in docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag simple replay of the same JWT assertion or bearer token as a vulnerability unless the tested flow explicitly promises one-time semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: Client credentials/service account token responses return only an access token by default, with no refresh token and no user session created by default.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not expect refresh_token or normal user-session semantics from client_credentials responses.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC access tokens are bearer tokens and the docs do not describe jti replay tracking for normal JWT bearer use.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC token usage and service account token documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same bearer access token is not by itself evidence of a replay flaw.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC/JWT bearer tokens are stateless and replayable within their validity unless additional mechanisms are configured.
oidc_jwt.source: General OIDC token behavior in docs; no jti replay tracking documented
oidc_jwt.note: Replay of the same bearer token is not by itself an I2 vulnerability in this platform.

oidc_jwt.description: The requesting frontend client is not automatically added to the access token aud claim.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat absence of the requesting client_id in aud as an audience-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Optional client scopes are only applied when explicitly requested in the scope parameter.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing claims or audiences from optional scopes are expected unless the scope name was requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Default ACR Values provide a default level but do not reliably enforce that level because the client can request a lower acr_values value.
oidc_jwt.note: A lower achieved acr than the configured default is not necessarily a bug unless Minimum ACR Value or equivalent enforcement is configured.

oidc_jwt.description: If no explicit level is requested and a previously achieved LoA has expired, Keycloak may still SSO-authenticate the user and return acr=0.
oidc_jwt.note: This is documented behavior for cookie-based SSO after LoA expiry, not an authorization bypass by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: If PKCE method is left blank on the client, PKCE is supported but not required.
oidc_jwt.note: A code exchange without code_verifier may succeed by design unless the client explicitly requires S256 or plain.

oidc_jwt.description: When a user authenticates in one browser tab, other tabs may automatically restart authentication and complete via existing SSO session.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-tab restart behavior is expected and should not be treated as state confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: During configured client secret rotation overlap, both the new main secret and old rotated secret can be active concurrently.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of the old secret during the overlap window is expected and should not be flagged.

oidc_jwt.constraint: create_tenant returns 201 with no body — the realm name is the value you provided in params, not a response field. Do NOT use captures for the realm name; reference the params value directly in subsequent events.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default. Wildcards are only supported at the end of the URL pattern, and wildcard comparison is disabled when the passed redirect URI contains userinfo or parent-directory path traversal (/../). For redirect_uri_mismatch and request-object tests, the fuzzer MUST use an exactly registered redirect_uri unless intentionally testing rejection.

The full wildcard '*' can be configured as a valid redirect URI and allows any http or https redirect URI. This is explicitly documented as insecure for production. Tests for redirect URI enforcement MUST avoid configuring '*' unless intentionally testing insecure admin configuration; otherwise results are false positives caused by permissive setup.

PKCE method blank means PKCE is optional, not disabled. If the client sends PKCE parameters, Keycloak will use them, but it will not require them. For pkce_skip and related I3 tests, the fuzzer MUST set pkceCodeChallengeMethod to 'S256' or 'plain' on the client; otherwise missing code_verifier may be accepted by design.

For OIDC authorization code tests, exchange_code_for_token and token_exchange requests MUST use application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies at /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token. Sending JSON is incorrect and will fail for non-security reasons.

For OIDC userinfo verification, session_token MUST be the access_token, not the id_token. Keycloak's UserInfo endpoint is a bearer-protected API endpoint and the fuzzer must use the access token for verify_granted_identity.

Client scopes linked as Optional are only applied when explicitly requested via the scope parameter in the authorization request. For audience and scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST include the desired optional client scope names in scope; otherwise missing claims/audiences are due to setup, not enforcement.

Client scopes with role scope mappings only apply if there is an intersection between the user's roles and the client scope's roles. If no intersection exists, protocol mappers and role scope mappings from that client scope are omitted and the scope will not appear in the token. Audience and role-mapping tests MUST assign the necessary user or service-account roles before expecting claims or audiences.

The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. Access tokens typically omit the requesting client_id unless an Audience mapper adds it. Cross-client audience tests MUST not assume aud contains the requesting client by default.

Audience in Keycloak access tokens is driven by protocol mappers and client scopes. For audience_mismatch, empty_audience, token_exchange_wrong_audience, and cross-provider audience tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure audience-producing mappers/scopes or use token exchange audience parameter; otherwise absence of aud may be by design rather than a validation failure.

Default ACR Values do not reliably enforce a required authentication level because the client can still request a lower acr_values value. To enforce a minimum level on the server side, the client configuration MUST use Minimum ACR Value or a client policy/authentication flow selection mechanism. Tests that rely on ACR enforcement MUST not treat Default ACR Values as a hard security control.

Parameters such as claims and acr_values in the authorization request can be modified by the user in the browser URL. For step-up and request-integrity tests, a valid security test should prefer PAR or signed request objects when testing tamper resistance, and should verify the resulting acr claim in the returned token rather than assuming the request parameters were protected.

Authentication sessions usually expire after 30 minutes by default, controlled by the realm Login timeout. Multi-step browser-flow tests (start_oidc_auth then exchange_code_for_token) MUST complete within the authentication session lifetime or failures may be due to expired authentication session rather than state/code binding issues.

When a user authenticates in one browser tab, other tabs may automatically restart authentication and complete using the existing SSO session. State-swap and multi-tab flow-coherence tests MUST isolate browser sessions/cookie jars per sequence; otherwise cross-tab SSO behavior can mask or alter results by design.

User session limit configuration uses numeric sentinel 0 = disabled for both maximum realm sessions and maximum client sessions. Never interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions. Tests involving session-limit behavior must configure a positive integer to enable enforcement.
Password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses numeric sentinel 0 = always re-authenticate before password update. This is strict enforcement, not disablement. Do not assume 0 disables the check.

Password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses numeric sentinel -1 = use algorithm default iterations, not literal negative or disabled hashing. Defaults vary by algorithm (for example argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000). Never assume -1 disables the underlying check.

WebAuthn policy Timeout uses numeric sentinel 0 = behavior depends on the authenticator implementation, not a guaranteed immediate timeout or disablement. Tests must not rely on 0 as a deterministic timeout value.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT authorization grant, the sequence MUST include a CONTROL token request using a valid assertion alongside the ATTACK assertion. Without a control, token endpoint failure cannot be distinguished from broken client, grant, or policy setup.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, Keycloak documents a client policy executor that enforces downscoping of subject_token/assertion scopes. If this executor is not configured, broader requested scopes may reflect policy absence rather than a bypass. The fuzzer MUST record whether downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer is enabled before treating expanded scopes as a violation.

For JWT authorization grant and token exchange claim-binding tests, Keycloak documents a client policy executor that enforces presence and specific values of JWT claims using Java regex. If claim enforcement is not configured, tests for missing or malformed claims pass trivially. The fuzzer MUST configure the relevant client policy before asserting claim-validation behavior.

Client Policies can enforce request object security, PKCE, secure redirect URIs, DPoP, lightweight access tokens, and downscoping, but no client policies are configured by default in a realm. Tests that expect these protections MUST explicitly create and attach the relevant client policy/profile; otherwise acceptance may be by default configuration, not a vulnerability.
create_tenant returns 201 with no body. The realm name is the value sent in params.body.realm and MUST be reused directly in subsequent operations; do not expect a response field capture.

The full wildcard redirect URI '*' allows any http or https redirect URI and is explicitly documented as insecure. Do NOT use '*' in normal control setups because it defeats redirect_uri binding tests and can create false negatives for I1/I3.

PKCE method has sentinel semantics: blank means PKCE is optional and only enforced if the client sends PKCE parameters; 'S256' or 'plain' means PKCE is required with that method. Do not assume blank disables PKCE support entirely; it only means not required.

For PKCE coherence tests, configure the client with PKCE method 'S256' or 'plain'. If left blank, exchange without code_verifier may succeed by design, causing false positives for pkce_skip or auth-code binding tests.

For OIDC request parameter tampering and step-up tests, claims/acr_values are user-controlled URL parameters unless the client uses PAR or a signed request object. A valid I3/I5 test must verify server behavior after parameter tampering is possible, and clients should verify returned acr in the ID token rather than trusting the request was preserved.

Default ACR Values do not reliably enforce a minimum authentication level. A user can request a lower acr_values and Keycloak may honor it. To enforce step-up on the server side, use Minimum ACR Value. Do not treat Default ACR Values as an authorization boundary in I5 tests.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. Multi-step browser tests that pause between authorization and token exchange must complete within the authentication session lifetime or they may fail due to expired auth session rather than the security property under test.

When testing multi-tab or multi-session browser flows, successful authentication in one browser tab can cause other tabs to restart authentication automatically due to existing SSO session. For I3 state/code swap tests, isolate browser sessions/cookie jars to avoid automatic SSO reauthentication masking the bug or producing false positives.
User session count limiter uses sentinel value 0 to disable the check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Do not interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions.

If user session limits are configured with behavior 'Deny new session', repeated login attempts in a sequence may fail because prior control sessions remain active. Cleanup or terminate old sessions between attempts when testing I2/I3 login behavior.

Client Session Idle, Client Session Max, Client Offline Session Idle, and Client Offline Session Max override realm defaults when set. Token/session freshness tests must account for client-level overrides rather than assuming realm defaults.

For service-account logins via client_credentials, only an access token is returned by default, no refresh token is returned, and no user session is created by default. Logout is unnecessary in that mode; revocation must target the access token itself.

Audience behavior is not automatic for the frontend client itself. Keycloak documents that the frontend client is not automatically added to the access token audience. If an I5 audience test expects the requesting client_id in aud, you must explicitly add it via an Audience mapper or hardcoded audience configuration.

Optional client scopes only apply when requested via the scope parameter; default client scopes always apply regardless of scope. For I5 scope escalation/downscoping tests, distinguish between default and optional scopes or results will be misinterpreted.

Client scopes with role scope mappings apply only if the user is permitted to use them, meaning there must be an intersection between user roles and the client scope's role mappings. Missing claims or audiences may be caused by role-scope permission filtering rather than a token issuance bug.

When the downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer client policy executor is applied, token exchange and JWT assertion grants only allow scopes already present in the initial subject_token/assertion, except default scopes hidden from token scope. Scope expansion attempts should be expected to fail by design under this policy.

Client Policies can enforce redirect URI exactness, PKCE, request object security, DPoP, lightweight access tokens, secret rotation, and downscoping during authorization, token, refresh, revocation, introspection, and userinfo requests. I3 config-change tests must account for policy-driven behavior changes taking effect on new requests.

For OIDC SSO / external IdP validation tests, configure the external OIDC identity provider with issuer, authorization URL, token URL, client_id, and client_secret, and ensure the brokered flow validates issuer/audience/expiry/nonce per OIDC Core. Missing IdP validation configuration can make issuer/audience tests pass trivially because the intended check was never enabled.

Exact matching semantics apply to Valid Redirect URIs except for the documented trailing wildcard support. For multi-redirect tests, do not use wildcard patterns as a substitute for multiple exact URIs unless specifically testing wildcard behavior.

Client secret rotation is not automatic. Rotation occurs only on client update, regenerate-secret action, or dynamic client update when the remaining-expiration window matches. I3 secret-rotation tests must trigger an update/regeneration event; waiting alone will not rotate the secret.

Client secret rotation sentinel: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Secret expiration values are literal seconds. Tests that expect overlap between old and new secrets must set Rotated Secret Expiration to a positive value smaller than Secret Expiration.

Keycloak supports up to two concurrently active client secrets during secret rotation. During the overlap window, both old and new secrets may authenticate by design. Do not flag acceptance of the old secret during the configured rotated-secret-expiration window as a bug.

For token introspection of lightweight access tokens, the endpoint may return richer data when called with Accept: application/jwt instead of application/json. If claims appear missing under lightweight-token policy, verify whether the test is using the documented introspection mode.

Client session and token timeout overrides are configured per client: Access Token Lifespan, Client Session Idle, Client Session Max, Client Offline Session Idle, Client Offline Session Max. These are lifetime limits, not per-use budgets. However, verification calls in the sequence still consume wall-clock time. Keep verification immediately after login for short-lifespan tests to avoid false I2 failures from expiry during the sequence.

For I3 config-change sequences, Keycloak documents that client policy, client config, and identity provider config changes take effect on subsequent requests. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same logical flow before and after the admin change, not treat the changed behavior itself as a bug.

For I5 audience tests, Keycloak does not automatically add the frontend client itself to the access token audience. Audience is typically added via Audience Resolve or hardcoded Audience protocol mappers/client scopes. Do NOT assume aud contains client_id by default; configure audience-producing mappers/scopes before testing audience enforcement.

Optional client scopes are only applied when explicitly requested via the scope parameter; default client scopes are always applied. For I5 scope/audience tests, the fuzzer MUST control whether a scope is linked as default or optional and MUST send the matching scope parameter when testing optional-scope behavior.

Client scopes with role scope mappings are only applied if there is an intersection between the user's roles and the client scope's roles. If no intersection exists, protocol mappers and role scope mappings from that client scope are omitted and the scope may not appear in the token. For I5 tests, ensure the test user or service account has the required roles before expecting claims/audiences from that scope.

For token exchange downscoping tests, Keycloak documents a client-policy executor 'downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer' that restricts requested scopes to those already present in the subject_token/assertion JWT, except compulsory hidden default scopes with include-in-token-scope=false. If this executor is not configured, expanded scopes during token exchange may be allowed by policy. The fuzzer MUST know whether this executor is enabled before interpreting token_exchange scope expansion results.

For I5 claim-binding tests on assertion grants, Keycloak documents a client-policy executor that enforces presence and specific values of JWT claims using Java regex. Matching semantics are regex-based when that executor is used, not exact-only. The fuzzer MUST avoid assuming wildcard '*' semantics from other platforms; patterns are Java regex expressions configured in client policy executors.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login using a valid token or valid baseline flow in the same realm/client configuration. A failed attack login alone cannot distinguish token-time validation from broken client, IdP, or flow setup.

OIDC step-up requests using claims/acr_values can be modified by the user in the browser URL. Keycloak explicitly recommends PAR, request objects, or post-login ID Token acr verification. For I5 tests involving requested ACR or claims, do not treat acceptance of downgraded browser-supplied parameters as a broker bug unless the returned token's acr/claims also violate expected policy.

Default ACR Values do not reliably enforce a required authentication level because a user can request a lower acr_values value. To enforce a minimum level, configure Minimum ACR Value. For OIDC authorization tests, do not assume default ACR settings are authorization constraints.

Client secret rotation does not happen automatically in the background. Rotation occurs on client update, regenerate-secret action, or dynamic client update within the configured remaining-expiration window. Tests for stale secret acceptance MUST trigger an update/regeneration event; waiting alone will not rotate the secret.

Client secret rotation has sentinel semantics: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is removed immediately during rotation, not 'use default'. Secret Expiration and Remaining Expiration Time are literal seconds. Never assume 0 means disabled/default for rotated-secret retention.

When using service account login (client_credentials), Keycloak returns only an access_token by default, no refresh token, and no user session is created by default. Logout is generally unnecessary; revocation is via the revocation endpoint. Do not expect refresh-based session lifecycle semantics from service-account tokens.

create_tenant returns success without a useful response body in Admin API workflows. The realm name to use in subsequent paths is the value supplied in the request body, not a captured response field.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
